text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler failed to add capacity in us-east-1 (gpu-cluster). Queue depth on /v1/generate spiked to 4200, median latency > 3.2s, GPU utilization 96% across pool. Autoscaler retries=3, max_nodes_reached=TRUE. Paging on-call: @alice.k.

alice.k: on it. joining bridge now. seeing lots of throttled requests in the proxy logs. starting quick triage — is this a flapping autoscaler or scheduling issue?

ben.sre: quick note: HPA triggered, but k8s show pods Pending with "Insufficient gpu". Looks like nodes have free GPU slices that are not being allocated due to MIG fragmentation.

carlos-mlinfra: confirmed. got partial output from scheduler: 
```
Scheduler debug: FailedBindings: 78
Reason: InsufficientResources (requested 1 x nvidia.com/gpu-1g)
Node gpu0: allocatable 8, allocatable-mig-slices: [4x1g, 2x2g] but reserved for other tenants, fragmentation prevents 1x4g mapping.
```
We have stranded capacity: multiple 1g MIG slices scattered but large model requests require contiguous larger slices or full GPU, so pods are pending even though aggregate free vGPU exists.

alice.k: ok that explains it. customers on support queue reporting generation timeouts. @dana-cs please compile impacted customers. We need emergency mitigation: 1) short term throttle/batch limits, 2) fall back to quantized/smaller model variant, 3) force-repack nodes or emergency MIG resize if possible.

dana-cs: on it. preliminary list: 5 enterprise tenants (ApexHealth, Clipware, Shoply, LexiDocs, MarketSigma) seeing 503s or very long tail latencies. I'm drafting a status note. Any ETA for fix?

ben.sre: attempting node-level interventions now. Plan: cordon a subset of nodes and perform fast MIG reconfiguration + kubelet restart to coalesce slices. Risk: short disruption to pods on those nodes (~30-90s per node). Need approval from @eva-engmgr for targeted disruption.

eva-engmgr: approved for targeted disruption on up to 6 nodes in us-east-1 if it reduces customer impact. Coordinate with SRE and ML infra. Keep CS posted.

carlos-mlinfra: doing a rolling sequence: 
1) drain node gpu-ue1-12 (evict non-critical workloads)
2) delete MIG device plugins and run mig-config to move to 2x4g from 8x1g where appropriate
3) restart node kubelet and re-register
This will free contiguous capacity for large model pods.

alice.k: while that's running, enable emergency routing: divert traffic of heavyweight models to dedicated-pool fallback (lower throughput but stable). Also push temp rate limit for non-paying tiers to 10 rps. Deploy-bot, please run the route switch.

deploy-bot: Executing route switch: 
- route /v1/generate model=redwood-13b-large -> dedicated-pool-us-east (populated by reserved nodes)
- apply rate-limit: non-enterprise=10rps
Status: in_progress

incident-bot: UPDATE: queue depth decreasing from 4200 -> 1800 after routing changes, but still higher than normal. New Pending pods still ~24.

ben.sre: MIG resize step 1 done on gpu-ue1-12, node rejoined. Observed reclaimed contiguous 2x4g on that host. Scheduler immediately placed 4 pending pods. Good sign.

carlos-mlinfra: rolling through nodes 12, 15, 19, 23. Note: some nodes can't be reconfigured because workloads are pinned to specific MIG slices (persistent jobs). Those will need live requeueing or tenant migration — planning to evict low-priority batch jobs to consolidate.

alice.k: is there any risk of hitting autoscaler limits again while we manipulate nodes? We hit max_nodes_reached earlier.

ben.sre: autoscaler had a cap due to budgeted reserved capacity flag — we've temporarily raised the cap by 10 nodes for emergency. Cloud account limit is still under threshold.

carlos-mlinfra: additional mitigation: enabling scheduler binpacking override to prefer placing small jobs onto fragmented leftover slices. This will require a patch and restart of scheduler with feature-flag "allow-mig-overcommit" = false -> we're toggling thin-packing heuristics to be more tolerant. Doing canary to one control-plane instance first.

alice.k: good. also let's deploy a temporary admission webhook that rewrites large single-pod GPU requests into N smaller replicas that can pack into existing MIG slices for non-latency-sensitive workloads. Only apply to batch and background jobs.

carlos-mlinfra: webhook patch applied to canary, observed one batch job being broken into 4 smaller replicas and scheduled successfully onto fragmented GPUs. Looks promising. Will roll to all.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: high for ApexHealth and Clipware (timeouts, data plane errors), medium for Shoply and LexiDocs (slow tail latencies), low for MarketSigma (degraded throughput).

dana-cs: sending out customer notices: will confirm ETA after we finish rolling MIG reconfigs (approx 40–60 min). Message includes workaround: enable fallback quantized model and reduce concurrency.

eva-engmgr: after this incident we need 3 actions for long term: 1) scheduler improvement to be MIG-aware and pack small jobs, 2) autoscaler policy to detect fragmentation and prefer new full-GPU nodes, 3) migration tool to consolidate stranded slices. Please create tickets.

alice.k: agreed. immediate next steps: finish rolling MIG resize (target 6 nodes), enable binpacking override cluster-wide, maintain routing fallback, monitor queue. I'll stay on the bridge and handoff to night oncall at 1746003600 if still active.

ben.sre: rolling MIG resize completed on 5/6 nodes. One node gpu-ue1-23 had persistent workload that couldn't be evicted; scheduling still has ~6 pending pods. Queue depth now 350. Autoscaler now able to place new pods.

carlos-mlinfra: triggered final step: proactive eviction of idle batch tenants and consolidation job launched. Expected to free remaining stranded slices in 10–15m.

incident-bot: METRICS: latency p95 back to 1.1s from 3.2s, queue depth trending down to 120. No new 503 spikes in last 5m.

dana-cs: customer update sent for enterprise tenants with note about mitigations and expected full recovery in 30–45m.

aleve???: (minor typo) ignore

eva-engmgr: good work. please file postmortem with timeline, root cause analysis (MIG fragmentation + scheduler heuristics + autoscaler cap) and action items. Prioritize scheduler changes and a non-disruptive consolidation workflow.

alice.k: will own the postmortem. adding follow-ups: PM to own capacity budgeting review, infra to implement consolidation tool, SRE to add fragmentation-aware autoscaling.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: at 1746004520 - queue depth normalized, pending pods dropped to 0, customer impact reduced to informational. Closing bridge. :white_check_mark:

alice.k: handing off a short notes packet to night oncall: 
- root cause: scheduler couldn't place new pods due to MIG slice fragmentation and some nodes configured with many small slices; autoscaler hit a configured max_nodes cap and did not request enough full-GPU nodes.
- immediate fixes applied: route fallback, temp rate-limits, MIG rolling reconfig to consolidate slices, binpacking override, admission webhook for splitting batch jobs, raised autoscaler cap.
- followups: scheduler MIG-aware packing (P0), consolidation tooling (P1), autoscaler fragmentation detection (P1), customer communication templates (P2).

ben.sre: leaving logs and debug dump in /mnt/incidents/1746001234/ for postmortem.

carlos-mlinfra: will open PRs for scheduler heuristics and the admission webhook.

dana-cs: will follow up with customers to confirm no residual errors tomorrow morning.

alice.k: thanks everyone. closing thread.
